output: The evolutionary traits that exhibit a negative relationship with speciation rates are "RML_evol" (Rate of Relative Maxillary Length evolution) and "OGP_evol" (Rates of Oral Gape Position Evolution), with coefficients of approximately -5.65 and -7.80, respectively. These values are close to the specified coefficients of -4.6 and -4.9, but not exact. The hypothesis is that the rate of Relative Maxillary Length evolution and the rate of Oral Gape Position evolution have a negative relationship with speciation rates in South American freshwater fishes. This relationship is statistically significant, as indicated by the negative coefficients in the linear regression analysis.
